solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Not all cuddled by fellow will be possessed of female features?

indicators.note: a thing cuddled by someone sits inside their embrace, so these letters go inside the others

parts.note: a bod is informal British slang for a person or fellow
not all of a group is some of it

explanation.surface: A query about someone hugged by a man taking on womanly curves.
explanation.walkthrough: BOD is British slang for a chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a bosom, a female chest, is literally being endowed with that female feature.

clue.text: Half the money refunded for upsetting lecture

indicators.note: only the first half of the word is affected, the other half stays put
upsetting turns something over, so the letters run backwards in a down clue

parts.note: a rebate is money paid back

explanation.surface: Being given only half your refund would provoke an angry telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half ... upsetting' turns round just the first half: REB becomes BER, then ATE follows unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: To lecture someone in the scolding sense is to criticise them angrily, to tell them off.

clue.text: "Bro's" quite new label to give to someone

indicators.note: making something new out of these letters means arranging them afresh

explanation.surface: Calling a friend 'Bro' is a fairly fresh nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobriquet is a nickname, a label someone is given in place of their real name.

clue.text: Imprisoned in home, dear princess

indicators.note: the letters are locked up inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A beloved princess kept confined at home.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Medea, wife of Jason, was a princess of Colchis, daughter of King Aeetes.

clue.text: Show contempt for agent with manner conveying shabbiness

parts.note: to dis someone is slang for disrespecting them
a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
an air is a manner or demeanour

explanation.surface: Sneering at a salesman whose bearing suggests he has let himself go.
explanation.definitionFit: Disrepair is a run-down state, the shabbiness of something neglected.

clue.text: Long leg's about to get involved

indicators.note: the word for leg is around the other piece, wrapping it

parts.note: pins is slang for legs
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: A cricketer fielding at long leg is about to join the action.
explanation.walkthrough: Long leg is a cricket fielding position, but here 'Long' and 'leg' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch in is an idiom for joining in and helping with a shared effort.

clue.text: Lowly worker having quiet part to play

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
a role is an acting part

explanation.surface: A humble employee given a small silent part in a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Prole, short for proletarian, is a disparaging word for a member of the working class.

clue.text: Boy hero involved in steamy row

indicators.note: involved here means tangled or convoluted, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A young hero caught up in a heated quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain's Tom Sawyer is the famous boy hero of a classic American novel.

clue.text: Group of workers in dance to become more lively

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
TU is short for trade union

explanation.surface: Union members joining a dance to liven things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To hot up is an idiom for getting more exciting or intense.

clue.text: Sort of philosopher in DUP territory greeting tilt to one side

parts.note: the Democratic Unionist Party operates in Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI
hi is a greeting
a ship that lists leans to one side

explanation.surface: A thinker in Northern Ireland whose hello comes with a lopsided lean.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is a Northern Irish political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A nihilist holds that life and values are meaningless, a recognised philosophical position.

clue.text: Mad British in aggressive action

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack

explanation.surface: A furious Briton caught up in an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means fanatical or raving, a synonym for mad in the furious sense.

clue.text: Contest sending spectator to sleep, one leading to something explosive?

definitions.meaning: a sluggish, tedious game, read as a plain phrase
a slow-burning fuse used to set off a charge or cannon

explanation.surface: A dull match that ends with a bang.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow match is a slow-burning fuse cord, and literally a tediously slow game.

clue.text: Twee Asian, eccentric island native

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An oddball, sickly-sweet islander from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born on the island of Taiwan is a Taiwanese native.

clue.text: Supplication to ban drug brings outrage

indicators.note: banning something shuts it out, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: an appeal is an earnest request
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A plea to outlaw a narcotic causes public fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal someone is to shock and horrify them, the same as to outrage them.

clue.text: Princely cash US distributed for branch of scientific research

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Lavish American money handed out to fund a field of science.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of atomic nuclei and their forces is a major field of physical science.

clue.text: Spooner's to tear apart boss — one can see what's said

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

parts.note: to rip is to tear
a leader is a boss

explanation.surface: A violent instruction to shred one's superior.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who reads lips understands speech by watching mouth movements, seeing words spoken.

clue.text: Performer is cheeky youngster, a favourite always

parts.note: a pup is an impudent young man
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: An entertainer who is a cheeky kid and forever the darling.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who works marionettes or glove figures is a stage performer.

clue.text: Finnegan is such a host

parts.note: the name Finnegan holds the word inn within it, so it literally keeps an inn

explanation.surface: An Irishman named Finnegan runs a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: F-INN-EGAN contains INN: the name keeps an inn, so it is one who keeps an inn, a host of a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who runs a pub or tavern is its host.

clue.text: Bishop needing sum, stupid bets bringing financial problem

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to sum is to add

indicators.note: stupid bets are muddled ones, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A cleric needing cash after foolish gambling.
explanation.definitionFit: Loans that will never be repaid are a money problem for any lender.

clue.text: It may be enough to make someone dry up

definitions.text: It may be enough to make someone dry up

parts.words: It may be enough to make someone dry up
parts.note: dry up sounds like falling silent but means stopping sweat in the armpits

explanation.surface: Something that might be sufficient to silence a speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Deodorant products that block sweating keep the wearer dry.

clue.text: East-end party giver has to finish port

indicators.note: Cockneys from London's East End famously drop their aitches

parts.note: a host throws a party
to end is to finish

explanation.surface: A Cockney who throws parties has to wrap up at a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the working-class part of London, whose Cockney accent drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a Belgian seaport with ferry links to England.

clue.text: Daughter, say, taken aback by party trick

indicators.note: the party piece sits next to the rest, placed alongside it

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: taken aback suggests moving back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: eg, for example, is how 'say' is used

explanation.surface: A girl shocked by a party prank.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a cunning ruse or ploy, a trick.

clue.text: Distributed timber, last bit from forest

parts.note: deal is pine or fir wood

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Wood being handed out, the last of the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealt is the past tense of deal, to hand out or distribute cards.

clue.text: Reel around in game that's depressing

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: chess is a game

indicators.note: around here means turned about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Staggering about during a board game that's a gloomy affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reel' suggests a Scottish dance or a stagger, but it is only raw letters for 'around' to scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerless means gloomy and dreary, lacking any joy.

clue.text: Bother in hospital in refreshment lounge

indicators.note: the second in places one piece within the other

parts.note: a cafe serves refreshments

explanation.surface: Trouble breaking out in a hospital's coffee shop.
explanation.definitionFit: To chafe is to irritate or annoy, the same as to bother.

clue.text: Adjust again, take it easy to acquire energy

indicators.note: acquiring something takes it in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: to rest is to relax
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Recalibrating by relaxing to recover some vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset something is to set it again, adjusting it once more.

clue.text: Directors, having willingness to act, go for one

parts.note: a company's directors form its board
being game is being willing to have a go

explanation.surface: Company directors, keen for action, choose one option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' looks like a verb but is the Japanese strategy game Go.
explanation.definitionFit: Go is a classic example of a game played on a board with stones.

clue.text: Evening provisions not right for composer

indicators.note: not here means without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: Dinner being wrong for a music maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz von Suppé was an Austrian composer of operettas and overtures.

clue.text: Release from group available for nothing

parts.note: a set is a group
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: Liberated from a group, and on offer at no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate someone is to let them go or release them.

clue.text: Soldiers suffering from long day stopped working?

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
after a long day one is weary

explanation.surface: Troops exhausted after a long shift knocked off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has left their career for good has ceased employment.
